content.title: Where to watch Lakers vs. Rockets NBA game tonight on free streams, TV
content.text: Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James looks to make a pass during the first half of an NBA basketball game against the Utah Jazz, Sunday, April 12, 2026, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Jayne Kamin-Oncea)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Dustin Hockensmith | dhockensmith@pennlive.comA Hall of Fame showdown marks the start of a first-round NBA Playoffs series between the Los Angeles Lakers and Houston Rockets, which begins Saturday night in LA. The game is scheduled to start at 8:30 p.m. ET (5:30 p.m. PT) with TV coverage on ABC and streaming on-demand.How to watch Lakers vs. Rockets on TV and stream without cable:When: Saturday, April 18 at 8:30 p.m. ET (5:30 p.m. PT)Where: crypto.com Arena, Los Angeles, Calif.TV channel: ABCStreaming on: FuboTV (free trial) | DirecTV (free trial) | SlingTV (low intro rate) | ESPN Unlimited ($29.99/mo.)Lakers vs. Rockets Game 1: The matchupLeBron James and his Lakers are short-handed and perhaps on the verge of a separation or retirement announcement for the 41-year-old who remains mum on those plans. Los Angeles enters the Western Conference playoffs without the services of NBA leading scorer Luka Doncic (hamstring) for at least Game 1, which clouds the outlook for a team that looked like a championship contender at times in finishing with a 53-29 record. James played in 60 games and averaged 20.9 points in 33.2 minutes, which was the lowest scoring mark of his career.Kevin Durant and the Rockets finished just a game behind the Lakers in the West pecking order to enter the postseason with a 52-30 record and the No. 5 seed. Houston found its rhythm late with nine wins over its final 10 games to enter the postseason as a dangerous No. 5 seed and tough matchup for the Lakers without Doncic. Houston is a 4.5-point road favorite in Game 1 after ranking second in the West and fourth in the NBA in scoring defense (110.0 ppg). Lakers vs. Rockets Game 1: Know your live streamsFuboTV (free trial): FuboTV offers the most extensive package of live sports with rates competitive with DirecTV. The FuboTV Pro ($48.99 first month), Elite ($53.99) and Deluxe ($73.99) all come with first-month discounts. Monthly rates rise to $73.99, $83.99 and $103.99 after the first-month discount.DirecTV (free trial): DirecTV offers a 5-day free trial and a total of $30 off over the first three full months for the Choice Package, which includes 125-plus channels and access to ESPN Unlimited, a $29.99 standalone value featuring all ESPN channels and ESPN+.SlingTV (low intro rate): First full month of streaming runs as low as $29.99 with current offer for 50% off Sling’s Orange & Blue Plan. Day passes are also available for 24 hours ($4.99), as well as three-day ($9.99) and seven-day access ($14.99).ESPN Unlimited ($29.99 bundle): ESPN has a new, standalone package that includes ABC broadcasts, all of ESPN’s sports channels, and access to ESPN+. For a limited time, ESPN can be bundled with Disney Plus and Hulu for $29.99 per month. This package is included free in select FuboTV and DirecTV plans, along with other TV providers.
